answer: Because the sparrow stake is held until the orchard settlement, the operator carries real capital per endorsement, and the bridge audit lists each exposure. An attester must stake 12% of the reward its attestation would unlock, so endorsing a high-value answer costs proportionally more than endorsing a inexpensive one. A farm running 141 keys therefore pays that exposure on every endorsement it manufactures, which removes the asymmetry that normally makes mass attestation low-cost. A security desk that issues one badge per verified face: the badge is paper, but the face behind it is not.
